title: Circle C Ranch
desc: A full outdoor transformation with artificial turf, custom Cor-Ten steel work, and integrated landscape design.

details.Services: Artificial Turf, Steel Work, Landscape Design

about: The Circle C Ranch family wanted a yard that could keep up with their lifestyle, a space that required less maintenance, looked great year-round, and gave them more time to actually enjoy being outside. The existing yard was functional but uninspired: patchy grass, undefined borders, and no clear sense of purpose.

Our solution combined three key elements: a full artificial turf installation for a lush, zero-maintenance lawn; custom Cor-Ten steel work for structure and visual interest; and a thoughtful landscape design that tied everything together. The steel elements, including a planter screen and border details, add warmth and texture that complement the clean lines of the turf.
The result is a yard that feels intentional and complete. The family now has a beautiful outdoor space that requires minimal upkeep and delivers maximum enjoyment, exactly what they asked for.

desc: Limestone patio, custom seating wall, drought-tolerant native planting design, and full LED lighting throughout.

about: Glenn came to us wanting a backyard that could handle both family use and Austin's brutal summers without constant maintenance. The existing yard had poor drainage, sparse plantings, and no defined outdoor living area, common challenges for Southwest Austin properties.

Our team developed a layered plan: starting with the hardscape foundation, a limestone patio and integrated seating wall, then building out with drought-tolerant native plantings that would establish quickly and thrive long-term. Landscape lighting was added to extend the usable hours of the space well into the evening.
The finished space is a defined outdoor room that feels like it belongs to the property, durable, low-maintenance, and designed for real Austin life.

title: Circle C North
desc: Front and back yard xeriscape redesign with Texas natives, limestone pathway, and custom uplighting.
sub: A complete plants installation in Circle C North, a xeriscape-inspired plant palette with limestone hardscape and custom LED lighting.
about: Dan reached out wanting a landscape that reflected the character of his Travis Heights neighborhood, distinctive, mature-feeling, and water-wise. The original lawn required constant input to survive Austin summers, and he was ready to invest in something more durable and beautiful.

We developed a xeriscape-inspired design centered on Texas natives and adaptive perennials, plants selected to look better with each passing season rather than requiring replacement. A limestone pathway and entry feature tied the front together, while custom uplighting brought the property to life after dark.
The result is a landscape that reflects both the personality of the home and the intelligence of designing for Austin's specific climate, not against it.

This project showcases the beauty and functionality of xeriscaping, demonstrating how thoughtful design and native plants can create a stunning, sustainable landscape. The use of limestone not only ties in with the natural geology of the area but also provides a durable, low-maintenance solution for hardscaping. The strategic placement of LED lighting highlights the architectural features of the home and the intricate details of the landscape, creating a magical atmosphere in the evenings.

desc: Small yards require even more intentional design than large ones, every square foot has to work. This compact Austin backyard was redesigned from scratch to maximize usability, visual depth, and character within a tight footprint.

about: Small yards require even more intentional design than large ones, every square foot has to work. This compact Austin backyard was redesigned from scratch to maximize usability, visual depth, and character within a tight footprint.

The challenge was to create distinct zones, seating, planting, pathway, without the space feeling cramped or cluttered. We achieved this through careful material selection, vertical interest, and a plant palette that adds depth without overwhelming the boundaries.

The result is a space that feels larger than its dimensions, with layered planting, clean hardscape edges, and materials that feel native to Central Texas. It's proof that you don't need a sprawling property to have a stunning outdoor space.
